whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Defective Product Claim

items.title: You Often Don't Need to Prove Negligence
items.desc: California generally applies strict liability to defective products, so an injured person usually needs to show the product was defective and that it caused harm — not that the manufacturer was careless.

items.title: Multiple Parties Can Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers may all be liable depending on how the product moved through the chain of commerce, which can open up more than one avenue for recovery.

items.title: Keeping the Product Matters
items.desc: Because the product itself is often central evidence in a defect claim, an attorney can advise on how to preserve it properly before it's lost, discarded, or altered.

items.question: What counts as a 'defective' product under California law?
items.answer: There are generally three types: a design defect (the product is unreasonably dangerous even if made correctly), a manufacturing defect (something went wrong in production), or a warning defect (inadequate instructions or safety warnings). An attorney can help figure out which category applies to your situation and what evidence supports it.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, meaning you typically need to show the product was defective and caused your injury, not that the company was careless. This can make these claims different from typical negligence-based injury cases.

items.question: I was hurt by farm equipment near Rt 111 outside Brawley — does that change anything?

An independent attorney can look at the specifics of your situation, including where and how the equipment was used, and explain the options available to you.
